units.title: 1. Spinal Cord, Vertebrae and Segment Levels
units.guide:
Cord function is printed as motor output to and sensory output from trunk and limbs; length 45 cm; continuation of medulla from the upper border of atlas (C1) to adult L1-L2 or childhood L3-L4. Pia reaches the tip of coccyx; dura and arachnoid end at S2.
Neural tube forms in the 4th embryonic week; caudal tubular part becomes spinal cord. Spinal canal 70 cm; 33 vertebrae (C7, T12, L5, S5, C4); 31 segments (C8, T12, L5, S5, C1); roots are dorsal + ventral. Vertebra-to-segment offsets run same / +1 / +2 / +3 then T10 = L1,L2, T11 = L3,L4, T12 = epiconus, L1 = conus. The figure labels conus medullaris, internal and external terminal filum, cauda equina, dural sac termination and coccygeal nerve.

units.title: 2. Conus Medullaris, Cauda Equina and Root Values
units.sec: Conus, Filum, Cauda Equina & Root Values
units.guide:
Conus medullaris is the terminal portion of spinal cord. Cervical enlargement is C3-T2. Lumbar enlargement roots L2,L3; epiconus L4,L5,S1,S2; conus S3,S4,S5,C0. Filum terminale is pia to the tip of coccyx, length 20 cm.
Conus medullaris syndrome is B/L symmetric, roots S3-S5 & C1, motor weakness absent, B/L saddle anaesthesia, dribbling/incontinence (micturition centre S3,S4), absent bulbocavernosus and anal reflexes (patulous anal canal), tumour, insidious/acute (malignancy). Cauda equina is asymmetric radiculopathy of L2-L5, S1-S5, C1, motor weakness present, variable sensory loss, urinary symptoms only in extensive disease, absent and variable reflexes, disc abnormality, insidious.
Root actions: L1>L2 hip flexion; L2>L3 hip adduction; L4>L3 knee extension plus TA dorsiflexion/inversion and knee jerk; L5 EHL, eversion, hip abduction; S1 hip extension, knee flexion, plantar flexion, ankle jerk.

units.title: 3. Cross-Section, Myelopathy Types and Grey Matter
units.sec: Cord Tracts Cross-Section, Myelopathies & Grey Matter
units.guide:
Cross-section labels posterior column (cuneatus/gracilis), dorsal and ventral spinocerebellar tracts, lateral spinothalamic (pain, temperature), ventral spinothalamic (pressure, touch, minor role), ventral uncrossed corticospinal (distal limb, minor role), anterior horn, lateral corticospinal (pyramidal) with rubrospinal for distal limb movements, and vestibulospinal, ventral reticulospinal and tectospinal for axial and proximal limb movements.
Myelopathies are sensory/autonomic/motor symptoms d/t spinal cord disease. Compressive splits into intramedullary tumour (ependymoma, syringomyelia cavity expansion) and extramedullary disc compression; non-compressive is transverse myelitis. Above the lesion is normal (complete sparing); at the lesion based on anterior horn cells; below is motor (UMN) and sensory loss. Grey ventral column is AHC (α and γ). At the level: motor LMN, absent reflexes (maximum localizing value), sensory symptoms; L4 example = absent knee jerk plus knee-extension weakness, quadriceps atrophy and fasciculation.

units.title: 4. Dorsal Column and Lateral Spinothalamic Pathology
units.sec: White Matter: Dorsal Column & Lateral Spinothalamic
units.guide:
White matter is tracts/funiculi (funicular pain). Dorsal column is ascending: first-order DRG, fasciculus gracilis/cuneatus, decussation in medulla (internal arcuate fibers) via medial leminiscus to VPL thalamus, third-order to postcentral gyrus (3,1,2). Sensations: proprioception, fine touch, vibration, position and joint sense.
Brown-Sequard: I/L loss of posterior column sensations. Posterior compression (glove and stocking / cervical compression myelopathy) starts cervical (UL) and progresses to sacral (LL). Diabetic neuropathy is stocking and glove.
Lateral spinothalamic: pain and temperature; decussates in the cord 1 to 2 segments above; hemisection gives C/L sensory loss. Intradural/extramedullary lesion list: dissociative sensory loss, sacral sparing (cervical > sacral), suspended sensory loss, prominent early LMN features.

units.title: 5. Remaining Ascending Tracts, Corticospinal and Rubrospinal
units.guide:
Remaining ascending tracks: 2 spinocerebellar, 3 spinotectal, 4 spinoreticular, 5 spino-olivary. Lateral CST: pre-central gyrus → cerebral peduncle/midbrain → pyramidal decussation in medulla → lateral CST (and anterior CST) to LMN and skeletal muscle. Extramedullary lesion: early involvement; hemisection: I/L motor weakness.
Rubrospinal tract is the only extra pyramidal pathway in the lateral column; action flexion of upper limb. Decorticate (lesion above red nucleus, tract spared, UL flexed, LL extended) vs decerebrate (below red nucleus, tract affected, UL and LL extended).

units.title: 6. Ventral Tracts, Brown-Sequard and Blood Supply
units.guide:
Ventral/anterior ascending: ventral/anterior spinothalamic tract = pressure, crude touch (minor role). Ventral (uncrossed) CST = distal limb movements (minor role). Descending extrapyramidal: vestibulospinal, ventral reticulospinal, tectospinal; action extension.
Early descending-tract pathology: paraplegia in extension (CST); late: paraplegia in flexion (extrapyramidal). Brown Sequard: ipsilateral posterior-column loss and motor weakness; contralateral lateral spinothalamic (pain and temperature) loss.
Blood-supply figure labels gracilis, cuneatus, CST, rubrospinal, anterior lateral system, vestibulospinal, ventral spinal artery, dorsal spinal and radicular arteries, plus vertebral, basilar, anterior spinal, PICA, superior cerebellar, posterior spinal, ascending cervical, intercostal and lumbar feeders.

units.title: 7. Arterial Supply, Infarction and Denticulate Ligament
units.guide:
Origin is the vertebral artery. Two posterior spinal arteries supply posterior 1/3; one anterior spinal artery supplies anterior 2/3. Radicular (feeder) arteries reinforce from the lower cervical segment down. Artery of Adamkiewicz / arteria radicularis magna (largest) originates near T8-T12 and supplies the entire lower half. T4-T5 has fewer radicular arteries and higher ischaemic risk. Arteria vasocorona is the circumferential anastomosis; CST in the watershed → myelopathy.
ASA thrombosis: acute, generalized atherosclerosis, posterior-column sparing. PSA injury: traumatic accidents. Ligamentum denticulatum: pia attaching cord to dura; in compressive myelopathy it compresses the corticospinal tract.
